clue.text: The way to get rid of discomfort?

definitions.text: The way to get rid of discomfort?

parts.words: The way to get rid of discomfort?
parts.note: read as a remedy for pain, but 'way' is a literal road, one built to ease traffic congestion

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for a cure or method; the second reading makes 'way' a road and 'discomfort' a jammed town.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass built to take traffic away from a congested town centre is named for easing that congestion.

clue.text: Wise man will want to limit speed of modern times

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so the wise man's letters enclose the speed word

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
pace means speed

explanation.surface: A sage cautions that the hectic tempo of the present day needs curbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will want' is a link; 'to limit' is the container signal, the sage hemming in the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of space exploration, from the late 1950s on, is a common label for the present technological period.

clue.text: Already programmed before on TV

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Something recorded ahead of time to be shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A device configured in advance has its settings fixed beforehand.

clue.text: Wound that's right on one

parts.note: the mark left by a healed injury sits on the very person who bears it, on their skin

explanation.walkthrough: A light cryptic definition: the 'wound' in question is one that stays visible, right on you.
explanation.definitionFit: The lasting mark that a healed injury leaves is carried on the body of the person hurt.

clue.text: Put ban on wise men's conservative witchcraft

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as a trade union might black goods
the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity story

explanation.surface: A Tory bans the three kings' sorcery.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'black' goods is British trade-union slang for refusing to handle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery used for evil ends is the dark arts, the evil branch of magic.

clue.text: Snootiness upset Bern boys

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lads from the Swiss capital take offence at someone's haughty attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the letters of BERN and BOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking down on those thought socially inferior is snobbish airs, haughtiness.

clue.text: Cathedral clergyman keeps company of a junior one

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the clergyman's letters enclose the company

parts.note: a dean heads the clergy of a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A senior churchman employs a firm run by a lower-ranking cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the clergyman: 'a junior one' means a lower-ranking cleric, and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglican and Catholic orders the deacon ranks below the priest, a lower clergyman.

clue.text: Just a little lake

definitions.meaning: just here means only or nothing more than
a small lake or pond, especially in English place names

explanation.definitionFit: The word means only or nothing more than, and is also a small lake or pond, as in Windermere-type place names.

clue.text: By trying, one's replacing energy in Empire State

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter swaps in where another stood in the word

parts.note: taken as written before the change
E is the physics symbol for energy
one is the Roman numeral I
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Climbing the Empire State Building, someone swaps power sources experimentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the final E of EMPIRE for I. 'Empire State' looks like the New York building, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge gained by experiment and observation, by testing things out, is experimental rather than theoretical.

clue.text: Sister's girl showing ecstasy in new diamonds

indicators.note: in places the drug's letter within the diamonds slang

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A young woman revels in fresh diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside ICE, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling's daughter is one's niece, a relation in the next generation down.

clue.text: Awfully ironic about set-end nipper

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the extra letter
awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled
an end can be either extremity, here the opening letter of the word set

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a child's ironic comment at the close of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges IRONIC; 'about' puts it round S, the front end of 'set'. 'nipper' suggests a child, but here it is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A front cutting tooth bites or nips food, so it is called a nipper.

clue.text: Copper joins writer by the French cell

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a Bic is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A policeman meets an author near a French prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A small partitioned compartment, like an office booth or shower stall, is a small cell.

clue.text: Quick to eat European banquet

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the quick word swallows the letter

parts.note: fast means quick

explanation.surface: A hurried meal for a continental guest at a grand dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts E inside FAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate celebratory meal is a lavish dinner.

clue.text: Pen limper characters — one's in Baroness Orczy's books

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the phrase, taken as material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer with a limp creates characters for a baroness's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' treats the letters of PEN LIMPER as material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scarlet Pimpernel is the hero of Baroness Orczy's novels about rescuing French aristocrats.

clue.text: Bristly type isn't in lead -hurry!

indicators.note: in places the slang contraction inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
rush means hurry

explanation.surface: An impatient person who refuses to take the lead is told to get a move on.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash breaks the surface: 'Bristly type' is the definition, a tool made of bristles, not a prickly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool made of bristles is literally a bristly implement, a 'type' of one.

clue.text: Walk heavily over uncultivated land where there's rubbish

parts.note: to lumber is to move heavily and clumsily

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a moor is open uncultivated upland

explanation.surface: Someone trudges across rough land where litter is dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns MOOR into ROOM. A LUMBER ROOM is British for a junk storage room.
explanation.definitionFit: A room for storing disused furniture and junk is a British name for a box room.

clue.text: Sam stereotyping poor computer program

indicators.note: poor here means badly done, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Sam typecasts people in a weak piece of software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges SAM STEREOTYPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows or Linux is the core software that runs a computer and manages other programs.

clue.text: Come to life in river, carried along by the wind

indicators.note: in places the word for being born within the river's name

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
to be born is to come to life

explanation.surface: Something springs into being in a stream and drifts off on the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The AIRE is a river in Yorkshire, England, a crossword favourite among short river names.
explanation.definitionFit: Something floating aloft is in the air, carried by breezes.

clue.text: To run through fax isn't right anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow means haphazardly, so the letters fall in any order

explanation.surface: Someone stabs a fax machine that is not working properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' rearranges FAX ISN'T and R together.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or impale someone with a weapon is to run them through.

clue.text: Mark gives help over reviewer

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help
a critic reviews books, plays or films

explanation.surface: A reviewer hands out assistance and gives a grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AID into DIA. 'Mark' looks like a grade or a name, but is a sign on a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent or cedilla is a sign added to a letter to show pronunciation.

clue.text: Dire strait of painter

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, so the word's letters are badly rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist is in dire straits, as the song title has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dire' rearranges STRAIT. The surface recalls the rock band Dire Straits.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes pictures with paint is a creative practitioner of fine art.

clue.text: Sea dog had day with dissolute type

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man of loose morals

explanation.surface: An old sailor spent a day with a debauched companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea dog' could also be a seal; here it is the Elizabethan naval hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the famous Elizabethan seafarer and privateer, a classic old sailor.

clue.text: Party had old returns from trinket

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the words are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A partygoer gets back an old trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses HAD plus O to give ODAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingummy or whatsit is a word for some unnamed small object or gadget.

clue.text: Perform better getting gold, not hemmed in

parts.note: to outdo someone is to perform better than them
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An athlete beats the rest, winning gold out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in the open air is not confined indoors.

clue.text: Fearsome type therefore must be put up

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means raised, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A frightening figure must be tolerated, so it follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be put up' turns ERGO upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster of folklore that eats people is a frightening brute.

clue.text: Misshapen spoons to right of backer

indicators.note: misshapen means bent out of form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A supporter is handed some bent cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misshapen' rearranges SPOONS, with R to its right.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter who funds an event or a person is a financial patron.

clue.text: Unhappy about new building material

indicators.note: about means around, so the sad word goes round the letter

parts.note: sad means unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy over fresh supplies for the builders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SAD round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Granular grit is mixed with cement to make mortar and concrete.

clue.text: It comes from sap concerned with wickedness

parts.note: re means about or concerning
sin means wickedness

explanation.surface: A remark on the wickedness of a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sap' suggests a fool, but here it is tree fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticky substance that oozes from pine and other trees forms from their sap.

clue.text: Romanians are foreign here

indicators.note: foreign means strange or out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Visitors from Romania are outsiders in this little country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges ROMANIANS; read whole, the clue says Romanians are foreigners in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny republic inside Italy is a country where Romanian visitors are aliens.
